historical_record.description: The first building on the lot, a one-storey 20-by-20-foot cottage with rustic siding at the rear of the parcel, was built under a 1907 permit at a cost of $300.

The present house, in a different position and larger than the 1907 cottage, was built some time between 1914 and 1938 with no known permit; it first shows in a 1938 aerial photograph, and the original cottage may have been moved and absorbed into it.
Bought in 1955 by Daughters of Bilitis co-founders Phyllis Lyon and Del Martin, who wanted a house with a view; their longtime home and named as potentially eligible for landmark designation.
Phyllis Lyon took the telephone call here inviting her and Del Martin to join a handful of couples in starting a secret social club for lesbians, which became the Daughters of Bilitis.
The Daughters of Bilitis held a Halloween party here, announced at $1.50 a head in the calendar of the first issue of The Ladder; the house was a regular place for the group's meetings and parties.
On the opening Friday night of the Daughters of Bilitis's first national convention, attendees came to a cocktail party at the house.
A fire next door damaged the side of the house; Del Martin took a permit to repair it and replace the rustic siding and shingles.
A new concrete retaining wall was built across the front of the property, replacing the old one.
Concrete stairs and a chair lift were built up the slope to the house.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 292, Lyon-Martin House.

notable_residents.name: Del Martin
notable_residents.detail: Del Martin, co-founder and first president of the Daughters of Bilitis, lesbian-rights activist and author, lived here with Phyllis Lyon until her death.

notable_residents.name: Phyllis Lyon
notable_residents.detail: Phyllis Lyon, co-founder of the Daughters of Bilitis and first editor of The Ladder, lived here until her death at home.
